findings.summary: As first planned, `holdout diagnose` would have shipped DARK: the DIAGNOSE line was a write-only emitter (dropped by the _filtered_run_lines allow-list, no consumer), there was no --diagnose on-switch to flip, the command was undiscoverable (README + `run` never pointed to it), the dev-calibration use was a silent island, and the normalizer risked being a second copy of oracle().
findings.disposition: All five folded in: _filtered_run_lines keeps the DIAGNOSE prefix (holdout.py); --diagnose flag added to run_calibration and forwarded by the `diagnose` subcommand; README gained a 'Diagnose a run' section and `run --summary` prints a run->diagnose tip (suppressed when already diagnosing); --diagnose works for the public dev calibration too (the dev 'island' is resolved, not deferred); and the normalizer reuses the ONE oracle() via a parameter, not a copy. Wiring proven by tests (--diagnose accepted, filter keeps DIAGNOSE, subcommand present) and an EXERCISED test that emits a real DIAGNOSE line + DIAGNOSE-SUMMARY through run_calibration's main loop with a stub agent.

findings.summary: The draft would have built a diagnose-only normalizer plus a forked HEDGE/GENUINE bucket taxonomy — an Nth copy next to the standing ORACLE NORMALISATION PASS debt (which names oracle() as the normalization owner) and next to oracle()'s existing wrong-verdict-line/found-but-hedged/missed-entirely mode vocabulary.
findings.disposition: Unified on ONE parameterized scorer: oracle(scenario, output, normalizer=None), default None = identical scoring (preserves the deferred oracle-normalisation predictions). normalize_for_oracle is authored as the exact artifact that debt will later adopt as oracle()'s default — a pointer was added to the debt entry so paying it is 'flip the default + ledger + victim-sweep', not writing normalization twice. classify_failure CONSUMES the oracle's returned mode and layers only the one genuinely-new axis (would-pass-normalized), so there is no parallel taxonomy. Diagnose runs IN-PASS (reps[].out in memory, never persisted) — which is also the correct containment seam per the security review, not just a cost optimization.

findings.summary: The feature adds a new field (the classification label) to the holdout egress ALLOW-LIST — the boundary that keeps the private answer key (plant bodies, oracle regexes, raw doer output) out of any Claude-readable output. A leak here is the one catastrophe the holdout exists to prevent.
findings.disposition: Fresh-context security-adversary traced all five leak paths -> verdict CONTAINED: diagnose_line(scenario, label) structurally accepts only the already-public id/agent plus a closed-vocabulary label; classify_failure calls oracle(..., normalizer=...) and consumes the raw doer output as an in-memory boolean ([0]) that is never printed; the raw output is never emitted in holdout mode at all (scenario_detail_lines returns []); and _filtered_run_lines is the sole egress, an allow-list of line prefixes. Added the reviewer's suggested needle-pin: classify_failure over reps carrying all three secret channels yields only a closed-set label and a DIAGNOSE line containing none of them. No code change was required to close it; the label is the same information class as the already-public verdict/mode.
